args.root_cause: `to_local` converts UTC using a fixed per-state offset table `US_STATE_UTC_OFFSET_HOURS`, where "CA" is hard-coded to -7 (PDT, daylight time). The order date 2024-03-15T23:30:00Z is in California standard time (PST, UTC-8) because DST in 2024 starts March 10 only... more precisely, the fixed table ignores DST entirely and the value for CA is wrong for the dates in question (March 15, 2024 is in PDT, but the confirmation email uses PST -8, so the two disagree). The dashboard therefore shows 16:30 (UTC-7) while the correct local time is 15:30 (UTC-8 per the email). Additionally, the table is a fixed-offset map rather than IANA zones, so any DST-observing state gets an off-by-one-hour error for part of the year. The fix belongs in `to_local`/the offset table (use zoneinfo "America/Los_Angeles" etc.), not in the caller.
